dataset_uses.purpose: Generate distinct Ni species states (particles → clusters) through controlled thermal treatment under NH3 or H2

evidence.text: HAADF-STEM analysis revealed a large number of particles with sizes of 5−10 nm on the surface of the 10Ni/30La-CeO2 catalyst (Fig. 1a), which was treated with NH3 at 500 °C for 0.5 h. Further, only a limited number of Ni particles along with a substantial amount of Ni clusters were observed after being treated at 600 °C for 1 h (Fig. 1b, Supplementary Fig. 4). On this basis, the dispersion of Ni species was markedly improved when the treatment time was extended to 120 h. The metallic Ni particles were no longer detectable on the surface of the 10Ni/30La-CeO2 catalyst. A significant number of stable Ni clusters were observed, with an average size of 1−2 nm (Fig. 1c, Supplementary Fig. 5).

evidence.text: In contrast, after being subjected to the same treatments, the structure of the 10Ni/CeO2 catalyst collapsed, and a large number of metallic Ni particles with sizes of 5−10 nm precipitated (Supplementary Fig. 8 and 9).

dataset_uses.purpose: Validate thermodynamic and kinetic feasibility of Ni particle dispersion via Ni–O–La/Ce bonding and quantify interfacial energy evolution

evidence.text: DFT calculations revealed that the reactive Oads coordinated with either Ce or La atoms on the catalyst surface could establish strong MSI with Ni species, consequently promoting the redispersion of Ni nanoparticles (Fig. 4f).

This phenomenon can be attributed to the fact that when Ni atoms on the catalyst surface were directly bonded to O atoms in proximity to La, the negative adsorption energy (−0.75 eV) led to the formation of a stable adsorption structure.

dataset_uses.purpose: Comparative computational validation to demonstrate weaker Ni–O–Ce interaction

evidence.text: DFT calculations revealed distinct adsorption behaviors depending on the coordination environment of Ni. When Ni atoms formed direct bonds with Ce (Eads = 1.97 eV) or La (Eads = 1.71 eV) atoms in the support, the positive adsorption energies indicated thermodynamic instability. In contrast, Ni coordination with O atoms adjacent to Ce sites exhibited a lower adsorption energy (Eads = −0.26 eV), favoring stable configurations.
Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed that these effects led to a multi-layer Ni distribution on 10Ni/CeO2.

dataset_uses.purpose: Directly observe and confirm real-time structural evolution from Ni particles to clusters under operando conditions
used_fields: particle contraction → complete dispersion → retained highly dispersed state

evidence.text: In order to directly observe the formation process of these Ni clusters, in situ aberration-corrected ETEM was employed to characterize the 10Ni/30La-CeO2 catalyst. The nanoparticles gradually contracted when the temperature increased from room temperature to 450 °C under a H2 atmosphere (Fig. 2a, b). Then, the particles completely dispersed upon further increasing the temperature to 600 °C, and the highly dispersed state was retained even after returning to ambient temperature (Fig. 2c, d).
